name: rustd
description: drop-in cargo/rustc replacement for faster builds

paragraphs: rustd is a Rust compiler daemon. One process per user stays running, keeps rust-analyzer's analysis of your workspaces in memory and, when given a directory, compiled functions in a store on disk, and answers builds from that state. After an edit it compiles the functions that changed, with Cranelift or LLVM, and either links them in front of what rustc built or splices them into the executable that is already there.

cargo and rustc start from the file system on every build: they parse, resolve, type-check and generate code for a whole crate again when one function in it changed, and a second checkout of the same repository starts from nothing. rustd keeps that work. Git worktrees of one repository share one database, and a function compiled once is found again by the hash of what it was compiled from, in any workspace on the machine or, through an S3 bucket, on another machine.
It is meant for people and coding agents who build the same code many times, often in several worktrees at once.
features: through cargo rustd: --exclude, more than one --target, --message-format, -Z
a few language features, among them sym operands in asm! that is not naked, some
